description: Lawrencium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Lr and atomic number 103, named after Ernest Lawrence, inventor of the cyclotron. It is a radioactive metal that represents the eleventh transuranium element, the third transfermium, and the last member of the actinide series. Like all elements with atomic number over 100, it can only be produced in particle accelerators by bombarding lighter elements with charged particles.
uses: Lawrencium is most commonly used in chemistry through its isotope 260Lr, which has a half-life of 2.7 minutes and can be produced on a larger scale than the more stable 266Lr isotope. Chemistry experiments have been performed to study its behavior and chemical properties, including its reactions and ionic characteristics in aqueous solution.
characteristics: Lawrencium is expected to be a trivalent, silvery metal with a hexagonal close-packed crystal structure similar to lutetium. It has an estimated density of around 14.4 g/cm³, an estimated melting point around 1900 K (1600 °C), and a trivalent metallic radius of 171 pm. It is easily oxidized by air, steam, and acids, and chemically behaves as a heavier homolog to lutetium with an anomalous electron configuration of s2p instead of s2d.
